## Comparability caveat

Four of the five filers (Delta, United, Southwest, American) report clean, full calendar-year FY2024 results on a consistent basis [DOC-1]. **Alaska Air Group is not directly comparable**: it closed the Hawaiian Holdings acquisition on September 18, 2024, and consolidates Hawaiian only from that date forward, contributing $869M of revenue and a $113M net loss to the FY2024 figures [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 therefore blends ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of a larger, loss-making combined entity, and includes merger-period distortions. Its ratios below should be read as indicative only.

Also note the excerpts disclose only two expense lines (fuel and labor), not full operating expense detail [DOC-1], so total cost efficiency must be inferred from operating income.

## Fuel + labor as % of revenue (FY2024)

| Airline | Fuel + Labor | Revenue | % of Revenue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $10,566 + $16,161 = $26,727M | $61,643M | **43.4%** |
| United | $11,756 + $16,678 = $28,434M | $57,063M | 49.8% |
| American | $11,418 + $16,021 = $27,439M | $54,211M | 50.6% |
| Alaska* | $2,506 + $3,588 = $6,094M | $11,735M | 51.9% |
| Southwest | $5,812 + $12,240 = $18,052M | $27,483M | 65.7% |

All inputs from [DOC-1]; *Alaska affected by partial-period Hawaiian consolidation [DOC-2].

## Total cost structure (implied total operating expense = revenue − operating income)

| Airline | Operating Income | Operating Margin | Implied Opex / Revenue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $5,995M | **9.7%** | 90.3% |
| United | $5,096M | 8.9% | 91.1% |
| Alaska* | $570M | 4.9% | 95.1% |
| American | $2,614M | 4.8% | 95.2% |
| Southwest | $321M | 1.2% | 98.8% |

Operating income and revenue figures per [DOC-1].

## Conclusion

**Delta** leads on both measures: the lowest fuel-plus-labor burden (43.4% of revenue, roughly 6 points better than United and 22 points better than Southwest) and the lowest implied total operating cost ratio (90.3%), producing the highest operating margin at 9.7% [DOC-1]. United is a clear second. Southwest is the clear laggard, with labor alone consuming 44.5% of revenue and an operating margin of just 1.2% [DOC-1]. Alaska's apparent middle-of-the-pack position is unreliable given the Hawaiian acquisition accounting [DOC-2].

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — lowest fuel+labor share of revenue (43.4%) and lowest implied total operating cost ratio (90.3%), yielding the highest FY2024 operating margin (9.7%); note Alaska's figures are not directly comparable due to the mid-year Hawaiian acquisition.
